Description: Determine if the patient's anxiety is primarily due to the physiological effects of a substance, such as drugs, alcohol, or medications for any medical conditions. The criteria is met when the patient's mood disturbance is directly linked to the substance's effects.
Patient_Story: For the past few months, I've been drinking heavily, usually about six beers every evening to unwind after work. I noticed that on days when I drink more, my anxiety spikes, making me feel jittery and on edge, especially in social situations. Just last week, I went to a friend's party and ended up feeling so anxious that I had to leave early, even though I had been looking forward to it all week.

Description: Determine if the patient's anxiety mood is associated with disturbance in attention and awareness is characterized by a fluctuating course. The criteria is met when there is evidence of changes in the patient's level of attention or alertness that vary over time.
Patient_Story: Lately, I've noticed that my attention seems to fluctuate throughout the day. There are moments when I can focus on my work, but then suddenly, I'll find myself staring blankly at my computer screen, unable to remember what I was doing just moments before. This happened just yesterday during a meeting; I was engaged one minute, contributing to the discussion, and the next, I felt completely lost and detached, as if I was in a fog. It's frustrating because I can't predict when these lapses will hit, and they leave me feeling anxious about my performance.

Description: Substance Intoxication Delirium; Substance withdrawal delirium; Medication-Induced Delirium
Patient_Story: After a particularly stressful week, I decided to drink more than usual, about eight beers in one night, hoping it would help me relax. The next morning, I woke up feeling disoriented and shaky, with my heart racing and a terrible headache. I could hardly remember the night before, and I felt a sense of panic as I realized I had trouble even recognizing my own surroundings. It was as if I was in a daze, and I couldn't shake the feeling that something was seriously wrong.
